@@U00118@@
(A knock at the door.)

@@U00119@@
O death! I know that knock. My assistant. My life’s supreme moment destroyed. My wealth of vision interrupted by that plodding pedant! (瓦格纳, in dressing gown and nightcap, enters carrying a lamp. 浮士德 turns away in annoyance.)

@@U00121@@
Forgive me, I heard you declaiming. A passage, surely, from an old Greek tragedy? An art form I'd gladly turn to a profit, for nowadays, they say, it has its advantages. And I’ve often heard said a preacher could learn from an actor.

@@U00123@@
Yes, if the preacher himself is an actor— which happens from time to time.

@@U00125@@
Yes, well. But when a man is confined to his study, and never sees the world except on holidays, and then only at a distance, through a telescope, how is he to guide it by persuasion— the world?

@@U00127@@
If you don’t fee/ it, it’s a lost cause. It must well up from deep in your soul and win the hearts of your hearers with its primal energy. But, no, better you go on sitting there with scissors and paste,
translation:
@@U00118@@
（有人敲门。）

@@U00119@@
死亡啊！我知道那个敲门声。我的助理。我生命中最重要的时刻被毁了。我丰富的视野被那个笨手笨脚的学究打断了！ （瓦格纳穿着晨衣，戴着睡帽，提着一盏灯进来。浮士德恼怒地转过身去。）

@@U00121@@
原谅我，我听到了你的咆哮。肯定是来自一部古老的希腊悲剧的一段话？我很乐意将这种艺术形式用于盈利，因为现在，他们说，它有它的优势。我经常听说传教士可以向演员学习。

@@U00123@@
是的，如果传教士本人是一名演员——这种情况时常发生。

@@U00125@@
是的，好吧。但是，当一个人仅限于他的研究，除了假期之外从不看世界，而且只能通过望远镜远距离观察时，他如何通过说服来引导它——世界？

@@U00127@@
如果你不付费，那就失败了。它必须从你的灵魂深处涌出，并以其原始的能量赢得听众的心。但是，不，你最好继续拿着剪刀和浆糊坐在那里，
